item.title: CVE-2021-4034 · PwnKit: Local Privilege Escalation in polkit's pkexec
item.description:
TL;DR: When pkexec is invoked with an empty argument vector (argc=0), an out-of-bounds read treats envp[0] as argv[1], and an OOB write back into envp lets the attacker re-inject GCONV_PATH into the sanitized environment of a SUID-root binary. glibc’s iconv subsystem then loads an attacker-controlled shared library whose gconv_init() executes with EUID 0. No authentication. Deterministic. CVSS 7.8 (High).

1. Context — polkit and pkexec

polkit (formerly PolicyKit) is the authorization framework used by all major Linux desktop environments to allow unprivileged users to run specific commands with elevated privileges according to predefined policies. pkexec is polkit’s SUID-root binary: the only program in this chain that actually carries root privileges on disk.
